index_record.dataset_generation_caption:
The figure presents a two-part framework for GCN-based load forecasting with accelerated Shapley value-based model interpretation. The top section, enclosed in a blue dashed box, illustrates the 'GCN-Based Load Forecasting' pipeline. It begins with an input graph G(X, A), formed by combining meteorological factors X (visualized as a color gradient map) and spatial relationship A (a geographic map with red dots indicating locations). This input feeds into a representation generation model g, consisting of three consecutive convolutional layers (each depicted as a gray parallelogram with green circular nodes connected by black lines) followed by a pooling layer (a green parallelogram). The output from this stage, labeled R_G, is a green cube. This output is then concatenated with other features X_O (represented as a yellow cylinder) and fed into a forecasting model f, which comprises a fully connected (FC) layer shown as a neural network with five blue input nodes, four orange hidden nodes, and one orange output node. The entire top section is divided into two main components: the representation generation model g and the forecasting model f.

The bottom section, enclosed in an orange dashed box, details the 'Accelerated Shapley Value-Based Model Interpretation'. It starts with graph data G (a small green-node graph). This data is processed by a 'Mask Generator' block (yellow rectangle) using Monte Carlo sampling to produce an 'Edge Mask' (a stack of green binary matrices) and a 'Node Mask' (a stack of blue binary matrices). These masks are combined and applied to the forecasting model (light green rectangle) to generate a perturbed dataset (orange cylinder). The output of the forecasting model on this perturbed dataset yields time forecasts (a line graph showing load over time with multiple curves). These forecasts are then used to train a surrogate linear model (a scatter plot with a fitted line). Finally, the SHAP interpretation result is generated as a horizontal bar chart showing the contribution of each node, with longer bars indicating higher importance. A large downward arrow connects the top and bottom sections, indicating that the forecasting model from the top is interpreted using the method described in the bottom.
